title: Contact patch test in plane strain: two blocks with non-matching edges in uniaxial compression (implicit mortar contact)
source: The contact patch test: a contact discretisation must transmit a uniform pressure across a non-matching interface exactly; Taylor & Papadopoulos, On a patch test for contact problems in two dimensions, Nonlinear Computational Mechanics, Springer 1991, 690–702; passed by 2D mortar methods: Yang, Laursen & Meng, IJNME 62:1183–1225, 2005. Uniaxial stress between frictionless supports is uniform in both blocks

quantities.quantity: Small: σ_yy of element 4 over that of element 7
quantities.reason: small sliding is linear and its edge mortar integrals exact (degree-3 Gauss on the overlaps): the uniform stress is the discrete solution up to the convergence tolerance

quantities.quantity: Small: σ_yy of element 6 over that of element 7
Small: σ_yy of element 1 over that of element 7
Small: σ_yy of element 10 over that of element 7
Small: σ_xx of element 6 over its σ_yy (uniaxial stress: 0)
quantities.reason: a frictionless interface (and symmetry plane) leaves the blocks free to expand sideways; the non-matching interface must not hold them

quantities.quantity: Small: the contact pressure at the secondary node (0.5, 1) over −σ_yy of element 7
quantities.reason: the mortar multipliers are the nodal values of the contact pressure, uniform and equal to the stress across the interface

quantities.quantity: Small: the integrated contact pressure over the reaction at the pushed top
quantities.reason: the pressure carries the whole load across the interface (both are totals over the thickness)

quantities.quantity: Finite: σ_yy of element 4 over that of element 7
quantities.reason: finite sliding is exact up to the geometric terms of the gaps the augmentation leaves (10⁻⁵ of the element thickness) and the default convergence tolerances
